title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is from Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. The notation is consistent with the profinite completion G^ of the group G = <ρ,σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1>, which is Z/3 * Z/2 = PSL_2(Z) (the next page has ρ_G^3 = σ_G^2 = 1). Grothendieck studies groups M_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{ρ,σ}, B_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms u of G^ (together with auxiliary data a, b, U) that send ρ and σ to conjugates of ρ and σ, essentially up to powers. This is a PSL_2(Z)-flavoured approach to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group.

Previous page. To x = (u,a,b,U) in S_0M° he attached (α,β,f) = (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}, uU^{-1}) in G^×G^×G^. He also set ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ(β)^{-1}, with ρ(·) meaning conjugation by ρ, and introduced the twisted versions α_0, β_0, g, h.

Formula (59). The action of u on the generators is written in terms of these data:
- u(ρ) = int(f^{-1}α)ρ = int(f^{-1})(ξρ);
- u(σ) = int(f^{-1}β)σ = int(f^{-1})(ησ).
This is an identity once ρ(α) := ραρ^{-1}: then ξρ = αρα^{-1}, so f^{-1}αρα^{-1}f = int(f^{-1})(ξρ), and likewise for σ. It matches β_0 = f^{-1}β on the previous page. Read this way, u is 'f^{-1}-conjugation composed with the substitution ρ ↦ ξρ, σ ↦ ησ'. This is the same shape as a GT element acting via f and the exponent λ, here replaced by the cocycle-type elements ξ, η.

Remark. Grothendieck observes that the so-called 'fundamental hypothesis' (20) was used only through its part b). Without b) one must introduce
- Σ^eff_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Σ_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G^×G^, where Σ^eff is the set of pairs (ξ,η) for which some u in B_{ρ,σ} has u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ. These are the 'effective' pairs among those satisfying the defining equations (28) of Σ.
- Σ^eff is the image of B_{ρ,σ}, equivalently of SG_{ρ,σ} under the map (28), SG_{ρ,σ} → Σ_{ρ,σ}.
- (61) SG^eff_{ρ,σ} := the inverse image of Σ^eff under that map.
The earlier results then hold on SG^eff. A crossed-out sentence records that SG → Σ need not be surjective, its image being Σ^eff, and that otherwise nothing changes.

Purpose. This is bookkeeping to remove an unproved hypothesis, namely that every formal solution (ξ,η) of the 'loop equations' is realised by an automorphism. It restricts the statements to effectively realised solutions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Formula (59) is consistent with the definitions ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ(β)^{-1} on the previous page, provided ρ(·) and σ(·) denote inner conjugation.
Gap, acknowledged by Grothendieck: whether Σ^eff = Σ (surjectivity of SG → Σ) is left open. He simply restricts to the effective part.

ideas.what: Expressing an automorphism u of the profinite modular group as conjugation by f^{-1} composed with the substitution ρ ↦ ξρ, σ ↦ ησ
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of GT-type automorphisms of PSL_2(Z)^ (Lochak–Schneps / Nakamura-style action on the profinite modular group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura for PSL_2/SL_2 versions in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action on the profinite modular groups, but not these formulas

ideas.what: Distinguishing formal solutions Σ of the defining equations from effective ones Σ^eff realised by automorphisms; restricting the results to SG^eff to drop hypothesis (20b)
ideas.modern_name: Image of the automorphism group in the solution set of the GT-type equations (the lifting / surjectivity problem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the GT literature (e.g. whether solutions of Drinfeld's equations give automorphisms)

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether every solution (ξ,η) of the equations (28) defining Σ_{ρ,σ} is effective, i.e. induced by an automorphism in B_{ρ,σ}. This is the PSL_2(Z)^ analogue of asking whether formal solutions of the 'loop equations' always lift to automorphisms.
missed.quote: L'application SG_{ρ,σ} → Σ_{ρ,σ} n'est sans doute pas nécessairement surjective, son image étant Σ^eff_{ρ,σ}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small, concrete instance of the problem of comparing solution sets of GT-type equations with genuine automorphism groups. Taken alone it is a minor technical point.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical continuation: a conjugation formula that is a straightforward identity, plus a bookkeeping remark that drops a hypothesis by restricting to 'effective' solutions. It is of interest as documentation of Grothendieck's PSL_2(Z)^-based approach to GT-type objects, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: In (59), first line: 'int(f^{-1}γ)' should read 'int(f^{-1}α)'. This follows from consistency with ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}; the handwriting shows a struck-through letter.
In (59), the struck-through middle portions are false starts. The final forms are u(ρ) = int(f^{-1})(ξρ) and u(σ) = int(f^{-1})(ησ).
The symbol transcribed as 𝔖 is most likely a gothic G, denoting G^ itself; Σ ⊂ 𝔊×𝔊.
The handwritten page number at the bottom left is 514, the archive page.
